job.title: Product Lead (AI)
job.text:
Product Lead (AI)
Stealth startup — Remote-ish

We're a well-funded early stage team working on something big in the AI space. We can't say too much publicly yet, but we're backed by top-tier investors and moving fast.

We're looking for someone who can wear a lot of hats. You'll be involved in product, obviously, but also a bit of everything else — GTM, design input, maybe some hands-on work depending on your background. The right person is scrappy and doesn't need a lot of direction.

Location is flexible for the right candidate, though we do like to get the team together regularly.

Compensation is competitive and includes meaningful equity. Happy to discuss specifics once we connect.

(Fictional posting, written for this demo.)

recommendation_note: Note the search count: zero. The agent decided research could not move this answer, which is the behavior the eval suite checks for.
reasoning: The underlying role — first product leader at a funded early-stage AI company — is genuinely attractive if the company is real and well-capitalized. But nothing here is verifiable, and the gaps are the kind only the employer can close: who they are, what they build, what the scope actually is, and what the band is. Worth one exploratory conversation to force disclosure, not worth building an application against.
strengths: 0→1 ownership and comfort with ambiguity are a genuine match for early-stage product work
The breadth requested — product plus GTM plus design input — matches a demonstrated range
Early equity at a funded company is real upside if the company is what it claims
concerns: Scope is undefined: "a bit of everything else" and "maybe some hands-on work" describe no particular job
No compensation band, deferred until after contact
"Remote-ish" with regular gatherings could mean a de facto hub requirement
"Maybe some hands-on work" raises the risk of substituting for an engineering team
research_summary: No searches performed. The employer is anonymous and the posting contains no company name, product, investor or founder to search on, so no external lookup could change the recommendation.

agent_trace.message: Several material facts are missing: company identity, funding stage, comp band, team size, and what "hands-on" means. Missing information is not automatically a reason to search — the question is whether a search could close any of these gaps.

The posting names no company, no product, no investor and no founder. There is no searchable handle, and the remaining gaps — the band, the reporting line, the real location expectation — are things only the employer can answer. A search here would burn a call and return nothing that moves the recommendation. Not searching.

New York, NY · linkedin.com/in/sofia-tofigh/

June 2021 – October 2022 · Remote

- Technical consulting for Fortune 500 banking and insurance clients on multi-year Apache Kafka adoption strategies.

cover_letter:
I'll be direct about where I am with this one: I can't tell from the posting whether it's a role I'd be good at, because I can't tell what the role is. That isn't a complaint — stealth hiring is a legitimate constraint, and "we can't say much publicly" is a reasonable position for an early team. It just means the useful version of this note is a short one.

What I can say is what I'd bring to a first product hire. At JPMorgan I built an LLM evaluation framework from nothing, which mostly meant deciding what "correct" should mean for a generative product before anyone could measure it. Before that I owned a B2B marketplace end to end — supply integrations that automated 60% of deal flow, a mobile redesign that lifted engagement 127% at launch, AI-written listing content with guardrails that reverted to the original copy when quality was uncertain. That range is the thing that maps to "wear a lot of hats," and it's real rather than aspirational.

If it's useful, I'd rather have a short call than send a longer application. The things I'd want to understand are the ones the posting can't include: what you're building, what the first product hire actually owns, how big the engineering team is, and roughly where the band sits.

Sofia Tofigh

fit_areas: Genuine 0→1 range: discovery, evaluation design, and shipping across unrelated surfaces
Comfortable defining problems where no playbook exists
Technical enough to work directly with a small engineering team
gaps: The role is undefined, so fit cannot be assessed — this is the company's gap, not the candidate's
"Hands-on work" may mean production engineering, which is outside the profile
emphasize: Breadth backed by shipped outcomes rather than by claiming versatility
Willingness to operate without direction, evidenced by the evaluation work
avoid: Enthusiasm about a company whose product is unknown — it reads as unserious
Committing to scope before the scope is defined
